titulo: Just in case, to top it all
intro: Por and para at B2: the contrasts that change the meaning, and the fixed phrases.
p.por poco.nota: Por poco me caigo: I nearly fell. Spanish uses the present.
p.no es para tanto: it's not such a big deal
b1.texto:
**Por** looks at what lies behind: the cause (por amor), the doer (escrito **por**), the exchange (lo compré **por** diez euros), on someone's behalf (hazlo **por** mí), the way through (**por** el parque), rough time and place (**por** la mañana, **por** aquí), the means (**por** correo), the rate (dos veces **por** semana), and what is still to do (queda mucho **por** hacer).

**Para** looks ahead: the purpose, the receiver, the direction (salgo **para** Madrid), the deadline (**para** el lunes), an opinion (**para mí**), an employer (trabajo **para** un banco), and a comparison with what you would expect: **para ser** extranjero, habla muy bien.

Minimal pairs: lo hice **por ti** (because of you) and lo hice **para ti** (to give to you). **Por mí**, vale (I don't mind) and **para mí**, es un error (in my view).

**Estar para** is to be about to, or in the mood for: no estoy **para** bromas. **Estar por** is to be inclined to, or still to be done.
b3.f0: You're here at last! I nearly missed the train.
b3.f1: Sorry. There was a traffic jam and, to top it all, I ran out of petrol.
b3.f2: Well, it's not such a big deal. Have you got an umbrella?
b3.f3: Yes, just in case. Apparently it's going to rain.
b3.f4: For someone so absent-minded, you've come very well prepared today.
b3.f5: As far as I'm concerned, we can go now.
b5.pregunta: Complete: I did it for your sake, because of you.
b5.o0.refuerzo: The motive behind the action: por.
b5.o1.refuerzo: Para ti would mean it was meant for you to have.
b5.o2.refuerzo: De ti would mean about you or from you.
b6.pregunta: Complete: for a foreigner, he speaks very well.
b6.o0.refuerzo: A comparison with what you would expect: para.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Por ser extranjero would mean because he is a foreigner.
b6.o2.refuerzo: De does not make this comparison.
b7.pregunta: Complete: there is a lot still to do.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Por plus infinitive: still to be done.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Para hacer would give a purpose.
b7.o2.refuerzo: A hacer is not used here.
b8.o1.explicacion: Por poco means nearly, and the present refers to the past.
b8.o2: I fell for a short time.
b9.pregunta: A friend suggests a film. You do not mind either way. What do you say?
b9.o0.refuerzo: As far as I'm concerned, fine.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Para mí gives an opinion or names the receiver.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That would mean for your sake.
b10.traduccion: To top it all, I ran out of petrol.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write the story of a terrible day, with por, para and at least five set phrases: por fin, por lo visto, para colmo, por si acaso…

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud what precautions you take before a trip, and why.
